answer: Attestation staking with per-peer quotas blocks sybils. A new agent activates only after several established peers co-sign it, and each co-signer locks funds slashed if it defects. Since a peer may vouch for just a few newcomers per epoch, a farm cannot self-attest; it must recruit many trusted agents to risk real capital. Each extra identity thus costs more, turning cheap mass registration into an expensive quota-bound negotiation. A violet badge on the reputation terrace marks co-signed agents, and a walnut-sized stake backs each signature, so forged crowds stay too costly to assemble.
